modelAnswer:
When Mrs.Meredith heard of John's idea, she thought it was a good one, too. "Bernard can keep all the money he earns," she said. That afternoon Harry watched the popping corn, John poured it into a big bowl, and Clara filled the paper bags. By evening, thirty bags stood in neat rows on the table. The next morning, Mrs. Meredith led the children to Bernard's home. When John explained the plan, Bernard's eyes lit up. "Do you really mean it?" he asked. His mother thanked them again and again, and Bernard found an old basket to carry the bags.

With everything ready, Bernard started out on his new business. At the first house he knocked softly and could hardly speak. But the woman who opened the door smiled and bought two bags. Feeling braver, Bernard went from street to street, telling people the popcorn was fresh and cheap. Some neighbors bought it because they liked popcorn; others bought it because they knew his family needed help. Before noon his basket was empty. Bernard ran home and poured the coins into his mother's hands. It was not much, but it was enough to buy bread and medicine for his father. That evening he came to thank the Merediths. John laughed. "There is plenty of corn left in Uncle John's box!"
